In computing , machine code is data encoded and structured to control a computer 's central processing unit (CPU) via its programmable interface . A computer program consists primarily of sequences of machine-code instructions. [ 1 ] Machine code is classified as native with respect to its host CPU since it is the language that the CPU interprets directly. [ 2 ] Some software interpreters translate the programming language that they interpret into a virtual machine code ( bytecode ) and process it with a P-code machine .
